newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES EASIER FOLLOWING TENDER.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES EASIER FOLLOWING TENDER.

text.p: Short-term interest rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted lower on Friday, tracking the treasury bill rate which came down at Thursday afternoon's weekly tender on the back of liquidity.
"The market is very active today. Most people are busy trying to buy treasury bills to adjust their statutory deposits (with the central Reserve Bank)," a dealer commented.

He said the tender rate for treasury bills eased to 17.94 percent from last weeks's 18 percent and that discount houses were on Friday selling the central bank paper in the market at 17.60 percent from 17.75 percent the previous day.

NCD bills maturing after 30, 60 and 90 days were also quoted softer at 19 and 17.85 percent (buying and selling respectively) from 19.50 and 18.25 percent while bankers acceptances were steady at 18.50 percent (buying) but easier at 17.60 from 17.75 percent (selling).
Call money shed half a percentage point to 17.50 percent in a market which opened with a Z$308.8 million surplus, up from Z$226.1 million.
